articles.title: A+E Doubles Down on Microdramas With Snips Partnership (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The media brand is working with the company to adapt traditional entertainment projects into mobile-first vertical stories, with episodes no more than two minutes long.
articles.content:
A+E is deepening its investment in the world of microdramas , most recently by inking a content partnership with the shortform video company Snips, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Under the auspices of the agreement, Snips will use its proprietary technology to adapt previously released television programs into mobile-first stories told in vertically oriented, short chapters, with cliffhangers galore, any extraneous material trimmed and episodes no more than two minutes long. The deal will allow the mobile app to stream roughly 50 true-crime and reality projects from A+E Global Media ’s library in this shortform format.

"A+E Global Media has built some of the most obsessively watched unscripted and scripted storytelling in the industry for over four decades, and true crime and documentary content is some of the most naturally suited to how people actually watch on mobile — in short, sharp, story-driven bursts," Snips co-founder and CEO Or Ben Shimon said in a statement . “We are delighted to bring some of A+E’s proven titles into our growing catalog.” The specific titles that will be adapted for the Snips audience were not immediately available.

The Snips deal will provide A+E, which will retain ownership rights over projects, with data on viewership, completion rates, monetization and engagement for specific titles on the app. Meanwhile, the projects provided by A+E will augment the entertainment library available on Snips, which now includes around 1,700 titles.

A+E Global Media is no stranger to the microdrama format, having first dipped its toes in the space in March when its label Lifetime released the project Tides of Temptation , executive produced by Taye Diggs. The company and Lifetime announced in October that they are releasing additional microdrama projects on MyLifetime.com and the Lifetime mobile app. A+E further revealed that it had adapted nearly 200 of its own projects into microdramas that the company would license to third-party platforms.

Snips has previously partnered with Banijay Rights and BIG Media to distribute microdrama adaptations of the latter companies’ projects.

“The idea of Snips, it's to be a platform. We're not creating our own content because we don't want to compete with our content partners,“ Ben Shimon said in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “The idea for us is that we're building relationships first [with] adapting content. Second, [our content partners] think about testing things or testing new genres with us."

For those uninitiated into the Sanrio community, the beloved character Hello Kitty is a little girl (yes, girl) who is five apples tall. On Thursday, she'll reach 107 apples tall when she takes flight (New York City weather permitting) as a balloon in Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade.

While a huge culture moment for Sanrio's Hello Kitty and Friends brand, it's far from the only major move the Japanese-based lifestyle and entertainment brand has been making around the world this year to connect with a wide range of age demographics and pockets of culture. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Extended Cut Sets December Release Date in Theaters Golden Globes: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Goes Comedy, ‘Dune 3’ Skips Box Office Achievement Category and More (EXCLUSIVE)

And it's been working: Sanrio achieved record results for the end of its fiscal year March 2026, reporting a 33.9% increase in sales year over year.

Created in 1974 by Japanese designer Yuko Shimizu as a cute character for Sanrio products, Hello Kitty has become a global brand that partners with major sporting leagues including the F1, MLB, NHL, NFL and top musicians like Bruno Mars and Katseye.

Along with all those tie-in products across everything from fashion to kitchenware and even several Hello Kitty-themed cafes throughout North America, there is a huge transmedia strategy in play at Sanrio, including multiple Hello Kitty video games (“Island Adventure” and the newly released “Party Land”), comic books, a digital series on YouTube and even a Hello Kitty animated movie made in collaboration with Warner Bros Pictures that's set to release in theaters in July 2028. And 18-34 is kind of this flywheel where they have families of their own or they have extended families, and they introduce the brand to a whole new generation. On the other hand, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, we believe, are fundamentally different from any other brand previously and that is they are digital natives.

When I grew up, my biggest influences were theatrical and maybe cartoon. Theirs are content on YouTube and gaming, and so subsequently, we go to where they already are. We think disproportionately gaming will be a big influence in the next five to 10 years. Because when we extrapolate the kids today and what they're doing with their time, maybe you go to a movie and you see it twice, maybe three times. You watch a TV series, you can see it several times. But when you play games, they're playing hundreds of times. So when they become captains of industry or ways to make decisions for a broader community, they're going to look at their influences and so that is the reason why we're in content, gaming, live experiences. Experiences are a big part of our brand, and fundamentally, because we believe that you cannot replace that energy of fandom outside of real life. And that's what brings people literally and figuratively together in a way that allows them to wear their favorite outfit or their favorite character and represent as part of something bigger than themselves.

Takiguchi: We've found unique ways to capture the imagination of communities in the market. We always try to be authentic in that way, so we don't necessarily follow the convention, especially in North America, where we're not predominantly a North American brand and our value is a little different from the North American thesis. I think it's a combination of a lot of things. We would have probably preferred to bring it out earlier too if we had the ability. But building this flywheel to the market was very important for us. Koch: We find too, like with all events, but sports in particular, our fans crave interacting together and going to an event together. With all the games, in a lot of cases, a lot of girlfriends will get together and that might be the one baseball game they go to all year, where eight of them will go together and it'll be like their special day out or family or dad and daughter. articles.title: 5 Good Movies That Actually Have Terrible Writing & I Can Explain Why
articles.summary: How many times have you watched a movie and loved it, only to realize later that many things in the story didn't really make sense? Hollywood is full of films like that. They bring a lot to the table, whether it's a great cast, awesome action sequences, or an appealing premise, but when it comes […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google How many times have you watched a movie and loved it , only to realize later that many things in the story didn't really make sense? Hollywood is full of films like that. They bring a lot to the table, whether it's a great cast, awesome action sequences, or an appealing premise, but when it comes to the writing, they fall pretty short . If you pay attention, you'll notice the story has quite a few flaws that may or may not get overshadowed by everything else the movie does well.

Yes, they can still be entertaining for all kinds of reasons, but calling it well-written is a different story. This list features 5 examples of exactly that: they're fan favorites, stood out for one reason or another, or are part of franchises that hold a special place in people's hearts . Even so, they all have writing choices that should have been reconsidered.

Don't get me wrong, F1 is a really good movie , and there's a reason it received positive reviews from critics and audiences, but delivering an enjoyable experience doesn't automatically mean the writing is just as good. The story follows Sonny Hayes (Brad Pitt), a former driver who gets the chance to return to Formula 1 decades after an accident almost ended his career. And this time, he has to help a struggling team while sharing the track with Joshua Pearce (Damson Idris) , a talented young driver who isn't exactly willing to take advice from him. And if you've watched a few sports movies, you can probably guess what happens next.

We have the veteran who needs to prove he can still compete, the rookie who needs to learn how to work with a team, issues within the racing team, and a rivalry that later turns into respect—it's all pretty predictable. And it's not that this formula doesn't work, but we've seen it plenty of times before. Also, there's the romance between Sonny and Kate (Kerry Condon), which doesn't help either, since it feels like the movie only included it because it needed a romantic subplot. I honestly think F1 would have been much better if it had spent more time exploring Sonny's past, the dynamic between the drivers, and even what goes on behind the scenes of the team. The racing sequences do a lot of heavy lifting , but a well-written film needs more than just cars speeding around a track, even when racing is the whole point.

As a Jurassic Park fan, I really wanted to like Jurassic World Rebirth a lot more, especially because it was supposed to bring the franchise back to its roots . And yes, it managed to do that, but it also forgot to properly develop and connect some of its storylines. Here we meet a team led by Zora Bennett (Scarlett Johansson), who travels to a remote island to collect dinosaur DNA samples that could help create life-saving medication. It's a cool idea as it allows the movie to bring back some of that sense of danger and exploration, and the dinosaurs and action scenes are genuinely good. However, the characters don't reach the same level .

The film also decides to focus on a family that gets stranded on the same island, which is a storyline that should add some emotional depth but seems like an interruption to the main plot. It's not necessarily a bad storyline, but the script doesn't give us a convincing reason for it to be there in the first place. So that means we have an unnecessarily large group of characters to follow when we barely have enough time to get to know the members of the main expedition. Mahershala Ali and Jonathan Bailey, for example, are both talented actors who could have done more with their roles, but the script struggles to give everyone enough attention because of everything happening on the island . And that's frustrating since David Koepp had already shown he knew exactly what he was doing with the original movie. With Rebirth , unfortunately, he dropped the ball .

Alien is a legendary movie franchise , but Prometheus showed up as a divisive entry. And honestly, one of the things that bothers me most about it is how confident and intelligent the script seems to think it is, even though the characters don't always act that way. The focus is on a group of scientists who travel to a distant moon after finding evidence that an extraterrestrial civilization may have played a role in humanity's creation. One of the highlights is Michael Fassbender's performance as David , and I actually think the overall concept is excellent, since it expands the franchise's lore into questions about religion, evolution, and AI. But the movie invests in raising philosophical questions rather than exploring them or building a satisfying story from beginning to end.

Besides, we're also talking about an extremely expensive scientific expedition involving professionals who were chosen specifically for their qualifications, yet the moment they reach their destination, some of them start acting as if they've never studied the risks of a space mission. We see Fifield (Sean Harris) and Millburn (Rafe Spall) get lost inside an alien structure despite the use of mapping technology, and others show very little caution when dealing with unknown life forms. And there's also the scene where some characters try to escape from a massive spaceship by running in a straight line instead of just getting out of its way. Prometheus is a great movie in terms of atmosphere and production design, but you can't take its story seriously .

I understand that Zack Snyder wanted to do something different with Batman V Superman: Dawn of Justice , creating a situation around someone with pretty much unlimited power who starts being seen as a threat. After the destruction of Metropolis in Man of Steel , Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck) begins to see Superman (Henry Cavill) as a danger to humanity and decides he needs to stop him before it's too late. But Clark Kent disagrees with Batman's violent methods and questions the way he treats Gotham's criminals. A cool idea in theory, right ? The problem is that the build-up to their eventual fight is far from convincing.

The story introduces several subplots involving Lex Luthor (Jesse Eisenberg), Lois Lane (Amy Adams), Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot), and the future Justice League, but it never gives any of them the development they need. And when the time finally comes for the two main characters to face off, we get that infamous scene where Batman is about to kill Superman but changes his mind after discovering that his enemy's mother is also named Martha. The idea is to make Bruce realize that his opponent is a person with a family he wants to protect, just like him, but the thing is that it happens so abruptly that it hardly feels like a meaningful emotional turning point. Basically, Batman V Superman tries to be deep and complex, but it just doesn't get there (not to mention Lex Luthor's whole convoluted scheme that nobody seems to catch on to).

You know how trying to please everyone isn't always a good idea? Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker makes that very clear. As the final chapter of the Skywalker Saga, the movie had the difficult task of wrapping up nine episodes and giving a satisfying conclusion to characters everyone had followed for decades. But instead of trusting the direction the trilogy had taken, it focuses on walking back previous choices and bringing back elements that some fans weren't happy with. The story follows Rey (Daisy Ridley), Finn (John Boyega), and Poe (Oscar Isaac) on a mission to stop Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) from returning. Somehow, he survived the events of Return of the Jedi and is now preparing a new attack against the galaxy— and that's where the problem begins .

The villain's return is never properly explained , and it completely changes the direction of the story, forcing the script to come up with a series of justifications for something that should have been set up much earlier. Plus, finding out that Rey is his granddaughter feels like an attempt to undo one of the best ideas in The Last Jedi : that she didn't need to come from an important family to play a crucial role in the story. I have no problem with changing direction, but those changes need to make sense, and in this film, too many decisions are just to address audience complaints. The pacing is also a mess, there are many convenient situations, and Finn and Poe don't get the character development they deserve . The Rise of Skywalker has too much going on at once, and it hurts the final result.

I'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments: Do you agree with me? Do you think any of these films suffer because of their writing, or are they still worth watching? And is there another movie you think should have made the list?

articles.content:
Ariana Grande has spoken out about the criticism she received for her "Petal" music video, describing it as an episode of "Black Mirror" but caveating that she "wouldn't change a thing" and "would put it out again today as is."

The pop star made the comments during an appearance on Las Culturistas podcast while discussing her latest album "Petal" and the visuals for the title track. In the video, which was released in August, Grande plays a character named Pepper who faces criticism from a panel of male judges as she auditions for a role, changing who she is to appease them. In the end, she snaps, brandishing a chainsaw in a murderous rampage as she realizes she doesn't need to conform to someone else's perception of her. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Oscars Visual Effects Top 20 Revealed: Disney Leads With Four Titles as ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Ramayana,’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ and ‘Wildwood’ Make the Cut (EXCLUSIVE) 'Cliff Booth' First Reactions: Brad Pitt's Sequel Is an ‘Absolute Triumph’ and a ‘Wildly Entertaining’ ‘Love Letter’ to Hollywood

Grande addressed the backlash to the video that, ironically, focused on her appearance instead of the message. "It's kind of like, when will it be about the art? When will it be about the work? That was largely what the video was about," she said. "It's like, oh here comes this girl. And there's always some distortion around the performance or art, whatever it is."

Subsequently, she said, "[It] had its own meta insane perception, and that was really interesting. But I feel so proud and grateful, I wouldn't change a thing. I would put it out again today as is, I wouldn't change a thing. I think my experience of putting art out and having people receive it is so different than how it used to be even just a few years ago."

Following the video's criticism, Grande released a statement declaring that she would be taking a "step back from visibility" after her "Eternal Sunshine" tour. In hindsight, she says, the backlash was something akin to an episode of "Black Mirror." "I really thought it was going to be a reveal, like me sharing a vulnerable… Like OK, here's this thing and then it happened sometimes 10 back," she said. "It was very funny and weird, but like I said, I love that project, I love that video. Those are two of my favorite videos, 'Hate That I Made You Love Me' and 'Petal.' I remember how it felt to be in the room, too, with all of those women dancers and all of us discussing what it felt like and what it held for us and we've all been told some kind of interesting thing about ourselves that has nothing to do with the art or our talent or our work or what we've given to our audition or whatever. articles.title: Dragon Ball Super Will Never Evolve Without Going Beyond Dragon Ball Z's Ending
articles.summary: Courtesy of Shueisha As long as Dragon Ball Super remains stuck within the ten year gap of time before the end of Dragon Ball Z, the story is never truly going to have the amount of freedom to explore its potential as fans might want. Dragon Ball series creator Akira Toriyama sadly passed away back in 2024, and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As long as Dragon Ball Super remains stuck within the ten year gap of time before the end of Dragon Ball Z , the story is never truly going to have the amount of freedom to explore its potential as fans might want. Dragon Ball series creator Akira Toriyama sadly passed away back in 2024, and it's left the franchise in a holding pattern ever since. While there is a new anime airing its episodes this Fall , and another now in the works, these releases aren't moving the story forward.

Dragon Ball Super' s manga has been on hiatus for the past couple of years without any signs of returning anytime soon , and it's likely because those currently behind the franchise are still trying to figure out a path forward. The rights for the Dragon Ball series are in flux as many notable studios and figures are in the mix, but once that's all settled it'll be time to move the story forward. But it's never going to be the kind of series fans might want as there's still an ending to eventually adhere too.

Dragon Ball Super has unfortunately sparked all kinds of timeline debates and confusion among fans ever since Toriyama returned to continue Dragon Ball Z 's story with the Battle of Gods arc. While the end of the manga imagined a future ten years after the end of the Majin Buu arc, Battle of Gods began to introduce new adventures within that span of time. While this had been an exciting prospect at the start, the more Dragon Ball Super continues the more it's apparent that it's eventually going to hit a brick wall as to how far it can actually go .

The Battle of Gods arc opened up the Dragon Ball franchise to an entirely new multiverse of ideas with 12 new universes full of potential allies or foes, Gods of Destruction that were the strongest beings of their respective universes, Angels that are even stronger than the Gods, and more as the scale and scope of everything increased dramatically from where Dragon Ball Z originally ended. Yet despite how much more infinitely the franchise can grow from this point on, it still technically has to fit within that ten year gap of time. It can never go beyond that ending.

Dragon Ball Super can never truly expand on some of its best ideas because it can never be a true sequel to Dragon Ball Z . Fans might continue to debate whether or not Dragon Ball GT was a successful attempt to continue the story without Toriyama, but unfortunately the franchise finds itself within that same situation once more as it moves on with new releases without its creator. And at least when it comes to Dragon Ball GT, it was able to move the timeline forward with its take on Goku and ability to play with ideas like Goku training Uub.

Working within this ten year time gap also puts an unnecessary limiter on what Dragon Ball can actually do with any of its future projects. It's why even Toriyama approved and created releases like Dragon Ball Daima ended up being marred by all sorts of other debates. It was a release also set right after the events of the Majin Buu arc, and that constraint just opened up a can of worms about which of the events were actually part of the canon even if they technically all are.

If the franchise has any hope for a future, it needs to be able to actually move into that future . Without Toriyama around, all of these Dragon Ball projects are going to technically both be a part of the canon and not at the same time anyway. But if Dragon Ball Super is finally able to move forward beyond End of Z and become a true sequel, then the literal sky is the limit for what it can do with Goku and all of the other characters. There will always be a ceiling on it otherwise.

That just seems antithetical to the Dragon Ball idea. It originally began with a young boy setting out on a magical adventure filled with possibilities and no limits on how far he could go. It eventually ended with the idea that Goku can pursue godly levels of strength heading into the future, but as is, he'll never truly be able to break that ceiling. There's only so much Dragon Ball can do right now as long as it continues to adhere by that unnecessary limit.

What do you want to see from Dragon Ball Super next? Do you want to keep the end of the timeline as is? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

Before Skydance (then Paramount Skydance) chief David Ellison hired Weiss in October 2025, she’d founded the online outlet known as The Free Press. articles.title: 5 Cult Animated Shows From 2009 That I Wish Would Come Back for More Episodes
articles.summary: 2009 was a light year for animated series debuts, and most of the ones that did weren't great or aren't cult classics. But there were many that returned for second or third seasons throughout the year. While they have all since come to an end, some of those shows have gone on to become cult […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google 2009 was a light year for animated series debuts, and most of the ones that did weren't great or aren't cult classics. But there were many that returned for second or third seasons throughout the year. While they have all since come to an end, some of those shows have gone on to become cult classics, taking on new life through reruns and streaming. While they didn't capture the love of the mass viewing public as shows like Phineas and Ferb and Star Wars: The Clone Wars (both of which premiered their second seasons in 2009) did.

These five shows on the air in 2009 were great and should come back for more episodes, though you might just be surprised by number one on the list.

The Cartoon Network series The Marvelous Misadventures of Flapjack premiered on June 5, 2008, and ended on August 31, 2010, originally taking life as a pilot and a series of shorts in 2007. The series followed the nautical marvelous misadventures of its titular character, a gullible young boy who was raised by a whale and mentored by an old pirate named Captain K'nuckles. Primarily set in the fictional town of Stormalong Harbor, the pair searched for the mysterious Candied Island. Flapjack was voiced by Thurop Van Orman (the show's creator), and Captain K'nuckles was voiced by Brian Doyle-Murray, using the same voice he used for The Flying Dutchman in SpongeBob SquarePants .

The Marvelous Misadventures of Flapjack ran for three seasons and 46 episodes, comprised of 90 segments. The first season ended on July 23, 2009, and the second premiered just days later on July 30th. The series never got the attention and praise that it deserved while it was on air. It was well written, funny, and even reviewed positively by critics. It even won a Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Achievement in Animation in 2009. Those who watched became fans, and they remained fans, developing into a cult following that keeps the show alive.

One of three television spin-offs of the DreamWorks Madagascar films, The Penguins of Madagascar followed the true breakout stars of the films: Skipper (Tom McGrath), Private (James Patrick Stuart), Rico (John DiMaggio), and Kowalski (Jeff Bennett). It aired on Nickelodeon and later Nicktoons from March 28, 2009, to January 4, 2016, releasing after the theatrical release of Madagascar 2: Escape 2 Africa (though a sneak peek did air in November 2009). Taking viewers back to the Central Park Zoo, the Penguins went on various missions within the zoo and occasionally beyond its walls out into the streets of New York City. The missions would often end up having complications as a result of the actions of King Julian (Danny Jacobs), Mort (Andy Richter), and Maurice (Kevin Michael Richardson). The two chimpanzees from the films would also often appear. It was never explained how they all ended up back at the Central Park Zoo

The Penguins of Madagascar premiered after the 2009 Kids' Choice Awards, a strong signal that the network had confidence in the show, likely bolstered by the success of the film months earlier. Nickelodeon even renewed the series for a second season before the first had even premiered. The series ran for three seasons totaling 149 episodes, with the second season comprising a whopping 68 episodes. The series was very funny and well-written. The Penguins, King Julian, Maurice, and Mort offered great comedic value and were just great characters in general. A return to this series would be a lot of fun.

A television spin-off of the hit animated film Barnyard (2006), Back at the Barnyard continued the story started in the film (while ignoring certain plot points that conflicted with the story they were telling in the series, such as Otis's love interest). It followed Otis (Chris Hardwick, replacing Kevin James from the film), Pip (Jeff Garcia), Pig (Tino Insana), Abby (Leigh-Allyn Baker), and more as they continued to go on adventures on the farm (and sometimes off of it) while still hiding their anthropomorphism from the farmer and others. That includes their nosy neighbor who wants to prove the animals can talk. The series was more comedic than the film, which leaned more into drama.

Back at the Barnyard premiered on Nicktoons on September 29, 2007. The second season premiered on February 25, 2009, the day after the first season finale. The series ran for two seasons of 26 episodes each, for a total of 52 episodes. While the film was successful, the series failed to capture the same popularity and was cancelled in late 2009. The final episode aired on November 12, 2011. Despite that, the series developed a cult following. It has been aired heavily in reruns on Nicktoons and NickRewind in the years since, and for a while was streaming on Netflix, proving it should have done better back when it was originally airing. This was a really fun series if you can get past the somewhat repetitive nature of it and dated animation, and it would be fun to return to that world with more episodes.

A very underrated series airing in 2009, Wow! Wow! Wubbzy! was a show starring anthropomorphic animal-like creatures based on the short comic The Tale of Flopsy, Mopsy, and Ted . Wubbzy was a yellow creature similar to a gerbil living in the town of Wuzzleburg. Voiced by Grey DeLisle, Wubbzy was a bit of an agent of chaos. He loved to play and would do that together with his friends Widget, the rabbit-like animal (Lara Jill Miller), Walden, who was similar to a bear (Carlos Alazraqui), and Daizy, the dog-like creature (Tara Strong). Episodes usually revolved around him devising some new way to do so. When problems would arise, he would turn to his friends for help.

Wow! Wow! Wubbzy! aired for two seasons of 26 episodes for a total of 52 episodes (just like Back at the Barnyard ). It premiered on Nickelodeon and Nick Jr. on August 21, 2006, and its second season premiered on September 2, 2008. It ran through 2009 until its finale on February 21, 2010. A third season was discussed but never moved forward. The series had become a cult classic in the years since its end, with childhood fans enjoying the nostalgia it brings. It had simple but engaging storytelling with a ton of energy that has become a bit of a lost art in recent years. It would be great to see it return in the future for new kids to enjoy.

The only Disney series on this list is Handy Manny , their competitor to Bob the Builder . This preschool-focused series focused on a repairman named Manny Garcia (Wilmer Valderrama) in the town of Sheetrock Hills. He was very friendly and could fix anything, even once repairing the trophy he would later receive himself. He did his work together with his living tools: Felipe the Phillips-head screwdriver (Carlos Alazraqui), Turner the Flat-head screwdriver (Dee Bradley Baker), Pat the claw hammer (Tom Kenny), Dusty the hand saw (Kath Soucie), and many more. Manny had a love interest named Kelly (Nancy Truman), who owned the local hardware store, but neither knew they liked each other for a long time.

Handy Manny ran on Playhouse Disney and later Disney Jr. for three seasons, premiering on September 16, 2006. It had 113 episodes split into two segments each for a total of 208 episodes. The second season premiered on October 27, 2007, and ran until October 4, 2009. The third season began just over one month later on November 7, 2009, and ran until the finale in 2013. The series had a great message and was quite humorous. The best running gag from Handy Manny involved Manny's clumsy neighbor, Mr. Lopart, who frequently tried to fix things on his own and would end up in some kind of predicament before accepting Manny's offer for help. Viewed by many as a rip-off of Bob the Builder , the series failed to reach the heights it should have, but is still remembered fondly by its original fans. Handy Manny deserves a second chance at life with new episodes to teach new young kids the lessons of the original.

Were you a fan of any of these shows growing up? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: As ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Opens on Just 200 Imax Screens, Netflix’s Movie Theater Push Is Still Failing Moviegoers
articles.summary: If you’re a fan of Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher and Brad Pitt, and you loved "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" and have your heart set on seeing that film’s sequel, the highly entertaining (and appropriately well-reviewed) "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," over Thanksgiving weekend, I have a scientific phrase to describe your […]
articles.content:
If you’re a fan of Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher and Brad Pitt , and you loved "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" and have your heart set on seeing that film’s sequel, the highly entertaining (and appropriately well-reviewed) " The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth ," over Thanksgiving weekend, I have a scientific phrase to describe your predicament: You’re shit out of luck.

But let me qualify that. If you’re lucky enough to live near one of the 200 Imax screens on which "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" will be playing, you can see the movie this weekend. Everyone else will have to wait until Dec. 23, when the film drops on Netflix. Sound familiar? It’s the old Netflix theater-and-streaming bait-and-switch, with the eagerly awaited movie in question being "released in theaters"…but also held back. (The film will play in theaters for just two weeks.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Daniel Radcliffe Is Unsure If He'll Watch HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ and Says the New Star ‘Doesn’t Need Any Advice From Me’ Nicola Coughlan 'Will Not Be Watching' New 'Harry Potter' Series Over J.K. Rowling's Trans Views: 'It's Not for Me'

We’re getting the slightly better version of the formula this time. For years, the Netflix game plan was to open a movie for an awards-qualifying run on an astoundingly small number of screens, the majority of them in New York and Los Angeles. The media tended to treat each of these "releases" as bigger than it was, for the funny reason that most entertainment reporters live in New York or L.A., which leads them to think, "Hey, it’s playing at a theater near me!" In the case of "The Further Mis-Adventures," perception may trump reality, as an Imax release has the aura of being something special.

In this case, the Imax release doesn’t hinge on the movie possessing some outsize visual magic. If anything, "The Further Mis-Adventures" represents the moment when the Tarantino aesthetic got fused with the karma of television . No, the Imax release is all about a deal that was cut months ago, after Netflix decided to bump the release of Greta Gerwig’s "Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew" from Thanksgiving weekend to Feb. 12, 2027. "Narnia" was originally set to occupy those 200 Imax screens (and only those screens), but Gerwig, using her post–"Barbie" clout, insisted on a larger-scale release. Ted Sarandos, the co-CEO of Netflix, caved on that one (Gerwig kind of had him over a barrel), and decided to placate the exhibitors by agreeing to swap "The Further Mis-Adventures" into the Thanksgiving/Imax slot. In his mind, that would make everyone happy. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"The Further Mis-Adventures" is being positioned as an Imax "event" — though here’s how Netflix, once again, has missed the forest for the streaming trees. The company has been through a dicey year, with Sarandos foiled in his attempt to acquire Warner Bros., which was a rare humiliating public defeat for him. And the fact that so many members of the entertainment industry questioned his commitment to theatrical was arguably why the potential deal didn't feel right. There was a fear in Hollywood that a Netflix/Warner Bros. merger could wind up killing the business of theatrical moviegoing as we know it. (Whatever misgivings one might have about Skydance or its leader, David Ellison, for some they represented the healthier alternative — or maybe just the lesser of two evils.) In the wake of that defeat, Sarandos declared that Netflix, going forward, would be pivoting more toward theatrical, on a case-by-case basis. What that would actually mean remained to be seen.

But the release of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" stands as a powerful indicator, because the desire to see this movie is so strong. In July of 2019, "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" enjoyed an opening weekend of $41 million. A highly anticipated sequel will tend to outperform the original film. That means that "The Further Mis-Adventures," had it opened on 3,500 screens (matching the screen count of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood"), could likely have netted at least $50 million, in the U.S. alone, over the five-day weekend. This raises the inevitable question: Why isn’t "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" opening on 3,500 screens? Imax is fine, but what about eyeballs?

The answer, in a way, is simple: That kind of release still isn’t part of the Netflix DNA. Netflix has the right to do what it wants as a business, but just stand back for a moment and consider, on basic populist moviegoing terms, the slightly absurd aspect of this situation, the way that it's simply not serving moviegoers .

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is an unusual Tarantino film, in that he wrote it and didn’t direct it, but it’s still every inch a QT joint. Fincher, who did direct it, has a powerful following of his own. (Their collaboration represents a rock-star mash-up.) And what of Brad Pitt, in the best role he has had in a decade — the one role that's ever won him an acting Oscar? Pitt is still a dazzling old-school movie star, and if you’re wondering if his highly publicized offscreen travails have hurt him at the box office, check out the grosses for his latest movie, "Heart of the Beast." It’s just a man-and-his-dog wilderness adventure film, and it’s coming up on a take of $70 million. Based on that, I’d say "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" would have killed. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The movie has a budget of $120 million, which raises the age-old question: Why is Ted Sarandos so willing to leave money on the table? But there’s now an age-old answer: That’s the way Sarandos preserves his business model. Let’s imagine an alternate universe in which Netflix released "The Further Mis-Adventures" on 3,500 screens, and by the time its run was over it had grossed $140 million (matching the domestic tally of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood"). If that had happened, prestige directors signing up with Netflix would be upping the pressure for full-scale theatrical releases. The whole era is now exerting that pressure, with sleeper smashes like "You Can See Everything," "Obsession," and "Backrooms" acting as a nearly mythological advertisement for the comeback of theatrical. The fact that Fincher himself, after years of working closely with Netflix (on "The Killer" and "Mank," and on the celebrated series "Mindhunter"), announced in September that he won’t be renewing his exclusive overall deal with the company is a move that feels hugely symbolic.

We’ll see what the further mis-adventures of Netflix bring. When it comes to theatrical, can Netflix truly change its spots? Much will be riding on Peter Rice, the company's new chief content officer. With his golden track record from the Fox Searchlight days, he has long been bullish on theatrical. If he hires Mike DeLuca and Pam Abdy, those high-powered refugees of Skydance, or even if Rice just oversees the film side himself (as he has suggested he might), it could mark a new era for Netflix. But based on the strangely limited release of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," a movie that audiences are hungry for but in most cases wlll not be able to see in theaters, I won’t be holding my breath, even as the constricted Netflix theatrical model now looks like it’s swimming perilously upstream.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Will Be Similar to GTA 6 in Quality Leap, Claims CDPR
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red believes The Witcher 4 can deliver a leap in quality comparable to the one between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6. The upcoming RPG is still years away, but the studio is already expressing confidence in how significantly it intends to improve upon The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. According […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google CD Projekt Red believes The Witcher 4 can deliver a leap in quality comparable to the one between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6 . The upcoming RPG is still years away, but the studio is already expressing confidence in how significantly it intends to improve upon The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . According to the company's leadership, players should expect a much bigger step forward when Ciri takes over as the series' protagonist.

The comparison came during CD Projekt Red's Q3 2026 earnings call on November 24. As reported by Video Games Chronicle , an investor asked joint CEO Michał Nowakowski whether the technological and qualitative leap from GTA 5 to GTA 6 could be comparable to the one between The Witcher 3 and its successor. Nowakowski addressed the comparison directly, making clear that the studio believes it can achieve a similarly substantial improvement.

Nowakowski was careful not to turn the earnings call into a detailed assessment of Rockstar's latest release. He acknowledged that CD Projekt Red had looked at GTA 6 and observed the differences between it and its predecessor, but brought the conversation back to the studio's own ambitions. When asked whether The Witcher 4 could make a comparable leap, his answer was affirmative.

"We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game," Nowakowski said during the call.He also pointed to the 11 years that had passed since The Witcher 3 as part of the reason players should expect such a substantial jump. His comments suggest CDPR is approaching the sequel as an opportunity to advance the experience across multiple areas, not just visuals.

The timeline makes that ambition uniquely interesting. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt originally launched in May 2015, while CD Projekt Red's latest earnings materials list The Witcher 4 for 2028. If that target holds, approximately 13 years will have separated the two mainline releases. That is a significant amount of time for technology and player expectations to change, giving the developer plenty of room to rethink what a new Witcher adventure can offer.

Still, Nowakowski's comparison should be understood for what it is: an expectation of a similar scale of improvement, not a hard claim that the two franchises will evolve in precisely the same way. CD Projekt Red has not laid out every specific upgrade players can expect, and the studio has yet to show the full scope of the finished game.

For now, the company's leadership is setting an ambitious target. Following one of the most acclaimed RPGs of its generation, The Witcher 4 has a particularly high bar to clear. CDPR clearly believes the next chapter can make the wait worthwhile.

articles.summary: Capcom has announced that it will be shutting down a multiplayer game that it just released back in 2023 in less than a year. Like every other publisher around the globe, Capcom has been looking to find wins of its own in the live-service space throughout this generation. Unfortunately, outside of games like Street Fighter […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Capcom has announced that it will be shutting down a multiplayer game that it just released back in 2023 in less than a year. Like every other publisher around the globe, Capcom has been looking to find wins of its own in the live-service space throughout this generation. Unfortunately, outside of games like Street Fighter 6 and Monster Hunter Wilds , many of Capcom's other attempts on the live-service front have been met with failure. Now, this is proving to be true once again, as the Japanese company has announced that one of its most prominent multiplayer titles of the past few years will be going offline in 2027.

Revealed in a new update message posted to its official website, Capcom announced its plans to shutter Exoprimal in the coming year. Released in July 2023, Exoprimal was a co-op-centric third-person shooter from Capcom that saw players taking on massive waves of dinosaurs. While it was in no way tied to the publisher's Dino Crisis franchise, the game initially drew comparisons to the dormant series (for obvious reasons), although it played and looked completely differently from Capcom's popular survival-horror games.

As for Exoprimal's shutdown, Capcom revealed that the game's servers will go offline next year on September 29th at 8am PT/11am ET. Prior to this date, however, Exoprimal itself will be taken off of digital marketplaces on March 30th. Effective immediately, Capcom has also pulled the Survival Pass off of storefronts, meaning that any and all premium tier offerings for the game are no lonegr available.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal," Capcom said. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

While it might be disappointing to see that Capcom is ending its support for Exoprimal , this move doesn't come as much of a shock at all. Upon its launch in 2023, Exoprimal was met with a rather middling response from both critics and players alike. This led to Capcom announcing one year after the game's release that it wasn't going to support it with any further content drops, DLC, or updates. Now, a little over two years after this news, Capcom is preparing to bring Exoprimal to an end entirely. As a result, those who have enjoyed the game and have continued to play it at times over the past few years now have only about 10 months left to do so before it, like the dinosaurs themselves, goes extinct.

How do you feel about Capcom's move to end its services for Exoprimal ? And does this decision surprise you whatsoever? Be sure to let me know your own thoughts down in the comments section.

articles.content:
Jane Fonda , Robert De Niro and Chelsea Handler are among the entertainment figures who have signed on to a letter backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in his bid to become Senate majority leader over Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY).

The letter, signed by about three dozen figures describing themselves as donors, fundraisers and artists, stated that in this year's midterms, "voters delivered not on ly a mandate but an opportunity for change: a government that delivers real value in the daily lives of working families."

"That change will only come from renewed leadership with a vision for the future," the letter stated. "The Democratic Party has a trust and credibility problem, and fixing it requires Senate leaders willing to challenge the entrenched interests and power structures that protect those in power, in both parties." The letter also called on senators to support candidates "who are dedicated to accountability, transparency and the bold agenda voters demanded." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); } Related Stories News Al Gore To Purchase Hometown Paper Carthage Courier News MS NOW Hosts Sign On To Letter Urging Adoption Of "Fair" WGAE Contract; Network Says Talks Are Ongoing And "Constructive"

The election for majority leader, to be held early next month, has highlighted party divisions, including among donors and in the entertainment industry, and even after the whopping victories of Democrats across the country in the midterms.

Noting that the upcoming vote on a Senate leader will be chosen by secret ballot, the letter called on the caucus to support Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer, the current minority leader who had been the presumptive favorite to win following Democrats huge gains in which they flipped control of the chamber.

Others who signed on to the letter include Bruce Cohen, Padma Lakshmi, Laurie David, David Mandel, Fisher Stevens, Marisa Tomei, Amy Ziering and Morgan Spector.

In a statement. De Niro said, "Americans voted for the change necessary to fight the corruption, cruelty, and policies of Trump and his Epstein class cronies. That's why I'm supporting change in Senate leadership. Chris Van Hollen is a progressive leader and a fierce fighter. He's the right person to lead the Senate majority." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Van Hollen has pitched his candidacy as a necessary response to the midterm results and that Democrats' unexpected gains were also calls for change, coming from the left and the middle of the party.

"The voters responsible for the Blue Tsunami want fundamental change and bold, new ideas. Simply put, Chuck Schumer is the past and Chris Van Hollen is the present and the future," Cohen said.

Schumer has insisted that he will emerge victorious, and even some entertainment industry observers believe that he will return to the post.

Mathew Littman, who leads The Working Group, which organizes Hollywood creatives, said via email, "Senator Schumer just led one of the great political wins of all time. He earned two years to lead his fellow Senate Democrats."

A Times analysis last week showed that Schumer had the public support of 16 senators and Van Hollen had the backing of 6, with 4 more calling for change. But more than two dozen senators' backing is unknown.

Spokespersons for Schumer and Van Hollen did not return requests for comment.

But a campaign aide to Schumer, Angelo Roefaro, told Politico that he was behind a bit of pranks-manship in advance of the release of the letter. He gained access to the Google doc draft of the letter and added Frank Sinatra's name to the list of signatories, and subbed in Schumer's name for Van Hollen. A Times reporter initially posted a copy of the letter endorsing Van Hollen, but with Sinatra's name still included, before replacing it with an image of the corrected letter, per Politico. Roefaro told Politico that Schumer was unaware of the prank.

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. Confirms "Science Bro" Replacements in Avengers: Doomsday, And It's Perfect
articles.summary: Marvel Studios The first big interviews and media profiles on Avengers: Doomsday are starting to hit, as we enter the final countdown to the epic crossover film's release. One of the latest featured articles on Doomsday has star Robert Downey Jr. sharing some of the finer details about the film and how his return as Doctor Doom […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The first big interviews and media profiles on Avengers: Doomsday are starting to hit, as we enter the final countdown to the epic crossover film's release. One of the latest featured articles on Doomsday has star Robert Downey Jr. sharing some of the finer details about the film and how his return as Doctor Doom compares to starring in the previous Avengers movie as Tony Stark/Iron Man.

One of the most unexpected fan-favorite moments of the original Avengers (2012) movie was seeing Tony Stark and Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo) geeking out together over alien technology in a SHIELD science lab. Stark and Banner quickly became the Marvel Cinematic Universe's signature bromance, under the nickname "The Science Bros." The Science Bros went on to be the source of Ultron and The Vision's creation in Avengers: Age of Ultron ; by Avengers: Endgame, they cracked time travel, and both used the Infinity Gauntlet to save/restore the universe.

Obviously, the original Science Bros' time is now done, but Downey has revealed that the tradition will continue into a new era during Avengers: Doomsday .

In EW's new feature on Avengers: Doomsday , Downey reveals more about how the film will establish a new "Science Bros" team in Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) and Doom (Downey). “We are the guys that always pick up each other’s FaceTimes, because we literally have just become a new version of science bros,” Downey said.

The film will apparently tap into traditional Marvel lore, in which Reed Richards and Victor Von Doom meet as the two leading geniuses at their university. They establish a deep bond, which (in comic lore) inevitably gets strained after Victor's insatiable ambitions for power leave him horribly disfigured, and he retreats into the persona of being an iron-fisted ruler hid behind an iron mask. “The love and respect that Doom and Reed have for each other in Doomsday is critical to the storytelling,” director Joe Russo said.

Fantastic Four: First Steps star Pedro Pascal further breaks down the MCU history between Doom and Reed Richards, confirming that these new science bros are more like polar opposites rather than collaborators with common ground. “Reed struggled to use his power of intelligence and understanding of science for the good of his family and the good of mankind," Pascal explained. "Whereas Doom, with equal, if not superior, intellectual power, uses it for questionable attainment of power. There’s so much delicious conflict there, standing on other ends of the spectrum.”

This entire discussion about Reed Richards and Doom's dynamic in Avengers: Doomsday soft-confirms one of the bigger rumors about the story: Doom isn't some arch-nemesis or even an antagonist at the start of the film; he's working with Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four to save the multiverse – or at least, save a portion of it that is ruled by Doom.

The descriptions from Downey and Pascal clearly reveal how Doom and Reed will be working together to solve the collapse of the Marvel multiverse – that is, until Doom sees an opportunity to grab the ultimate power of creating a new world for himself. The final Avengers: Doomsday trailer featured more scenes that seem to depict the moment when heroes like Steve Rogers(?) and Thor confront Doom about his true intentions and force him to shift into full villain mode, while Reed looks on in bewilderment, finally having to confront his old friend himself, asking, "Victor, did you do this!?" in response to some nefarious thing Doom has done. That also explains Sue Storm's (Vanessa Kirby) voiceover narration in a previous trailer, about knowing Victor but being unaware of just how "broken" he was, and how drastically he would react to multiversal calamity.

As I've said before: this may be the riskiest move Avengers: Doomsday is making with its story. Having Doom pretend to be heroic won't fool anyone in the audience, so hopefully it creates a more complex and compelling story as we get to know more about Doom and his true motivations .

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th. Ready for the next era of Marvel Science Bros?

articles.title: Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and ’70s, Dies at 87
articles.summary: People like her “don’t go away at all,” photographer Franco Rubartelli said. “They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”
articles.content:
Veruschka, the chameleonic, long-limbed supermodel and performance artist who photographer Richard Avedon once pronounced “the most beautiful woman in the world,” has died. She was 87.

Veruschka died in her home in Berlin, the German newspaper Bild reported.

On Instagram, her former partner and photographer Franco Rubartelli acknowledged her death and noted “she wasn’t just a great model. She was an elegant woman, sensitive, brave, with a beauty that did not stay in the camera, it would get into the soul of whoever watched her. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut Movies Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics' Circle Inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award

"She had a way of being in the world that you don’t learn; you take in. People like Veruschka don’t go away at all. They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”

One of the first supermodels, Veruschka in the 1960s and ‘70s appeared often on covers of Vogue and other magazines around the globe. With a high forehead, blue-eyed gaze and sculptured, distinctive cheekbones, she stood more than six feet tall and was a muse for designers including Karl Lagerfeld , Yves Saint Laurent and Valentino .

“What made the German model so mesmerizing was her seeming disinterest in preserving any one iteration of that beauty,” Anna Cafolla wrote in Vogue . “She could be imperious or impish, feral or feline, androgynous or opulently feminine. She could contort her impossibly long limbs into unreal configurations, traversing fashion magazines and the wider public’s consciousness with ease in a way that had never been done before.”

Vogue offers a look at her “most striking beauty looks of all time” here . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Veruschka did her first shoot wearing nothing but body paint in 1966, and after she left modeling in 1975, she collaborated with German sculptor-painter Holger Trülzsch for a series of avant-garde self-portrait photographs in which her painted figure dissolved into forests or sides of buildings.

On the big screen, she appeared as a version of herself in Michelangelo Antonioni’s Blow-Up (1966) when she’s photographed by David Hemmings’ character in London in the Swinging ’60s, and she had a brief turn as a high-stakes poker player in Casino Royale (2006).

Vera Gottliebe Anna Gräfin von Lehndorff-Steinort was born on May 14, 1939, in Königsberg, East Prussia (now Kaliningrad, Russia).

She was 5 when her father, Count Heinrich von Lehndorff-Steinort, was executed in September 1944 for his involvement in a plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler two months earlier. Her mother, Gottliebe, was sent to a prison camp as she and her three sisters were forced to live in a Nazi children’s home.

After moving from Hamburg, Germany, she was an art student in Florence when she was discovered in 1959 by photographer Ugo Mulas; before long, she was a full-time model, working in Paris, New York and Munich. She reinvented herself with a new name and returned to New York, where she found a champion in Diana Vreeland, then editor-in-chief of Vogue .

“I dressed all in black,” she recalled, “and went to see all the top photographers, like Irving Penn, and said, ‘I am Veruschka who comes from the border between Russia, Germany and Poland. I’d like to see what you can do with my face.’” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She appeared on 13 covers of Vogue ’s American edition and on the covers of its Italian, French and British editions as well. Along the way, she was photographed by the likes of Avedon, Penn, Rubartelli, Peter Beard, Francesco Scavullo, Horst P. Horst and David Bailey and became one of the highest-paid, most in-demand models of her generation.

She graced the cover of Life magazine in 1967, and a year later, Rubartelli famously shot her in a lace-up safari jacket from Yves Saint Laurent for French Vogue .

In 1971, she was the subject of the Rubartelli-directed fantasy film Veruschka — Poetry of a Woman and appeared in West German magazine Stern with 27 other women under the cover line “Wir haben abgetrieben!” (“We’ve had abortions!”) to advocate for making abortions legal.

She returned to the runway for Chanel in 1994, for Giles Deacon’s spring show in London in 2011 and for an Acne Studios lookbook in 2017.

Her autobiography, Veruschka — Mein Leben , was published in 2011.

Her beauty, Avedon said, “demands something, and you must extend yourself to meet the challenge or know that a kind of splendor is lost to you forever.”

articles.title: Told You So: Bake Off’s Semifinal Had An Issue I Called From Day 1
articles.summary: The writing was on the wall for The Great British Baking Show.
articles.content:
I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription . While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats , I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a big impact on the semifinals episode.

Unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had issues with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show , so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The studio behind hits such as Jujutsu Kaisen, Attack on Titan and more has a new Shonen Jump anime coming our way next year, and has dropped a new look at it ahead of its next big update during Jump Festa 2027 later this December. Shueisha's annual event is set to reveal a whole bunch of updates about all of the new anime and manga projects they have in the works for the next year and beyond, and that means we're about to get many new releases confirmed too.

Studio MAPPA, the studio behind Jujutsu Kaisen , not only has that franchise to worry about during Jump Festa 2027 , but there's also a new anime on the way also from the pages of Shonen Jump as well as Beat & Motion is set to make its debut next year. The anime adaptation for Naoki Fujita’s manga has dropped some special new art for the series ahead of the big event as it teases a new update is coming soon.

The anime adaptation for Beat & Motion was first announced to be in the works earlier this Summer, and it's likely that we'll get an update on what to expect from it during Jump Festa 2027 . Taking place over the December 19-20 weekend in Japan, the annual event shows off many of the new anime and manga titles that are in the works. Shueisha often showcases quite a bit during this time, and it often comes with new visuals, trailers and even more for some releases. That would be the perfect time for a new update on this series too.

Beat & Motion will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix sometime in 2027 , but has yet to confirm any concrete release details as of this time. The new series will be directed by Yuki Komada for Studio MAPPA with Misaki Morie providing the scripts, Kazunori Aoki handling the character designs, Takahiro Ogawa overseeing as animation producer, and dugout providing the sound production. It's also set to star the main duo of Shuichiro Umeda as Tatsuhiko and Aya Gomazuru as Nico.

Naoki Fujita's Beat & Motion is a pretty special series within the Shonen Jump library. It might have ended with only less than 50 chapters under its belt , but it was setting out to tell a small story that was able to come to its complete end. The creator won Shueisha's "MILLION TAG" reality show competition where they were seeking to find the next big creator, and as a result the series got its official serialization and this new anime adaptation with Netflix for its prize.

It's a story of two artists who inspire one another to pursue their respective dreams. One is an illustrator inspired by an up and coming musician, and the other is that musician who wants the illustrator to draw up a new music video for their song. It's a series that's bound to strike a chord when it hits, so how are you feeling about Beat & Motion so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has become the most popular comic company, something that basically began when they started their new superhero universe in the 1960s. While DC was sometimes able to compete with them, for the most part Marvel was on top. With success after success under their belt, the company decided to branch out, leading to the creation of the Marvel Cinematic Universe . Spider-Man, the X-Men, and the Fantastic Four's film rights were sold, so Marvel Studios only had access to the Avengers, their related characters, and the other portions of the Marvel Universe. The MCU hasn't been all about adapting books, but it has adapted some of the best stories in the company's history. However, one has been missing and it's about time it got an adaptation – Annihilation .

The MCU's first three Phases went in numerous directions, adapting various stories, with the overall story of the MCU being the battle against Thanos, who was out for the Infinity Stones. Since then, we've moved on to the Multiverse Saga, which is partly adapting Secret Wars . With Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars coming up, we're looking at what is (probably) going to be a new Phase. I think it's long past time Marvel looked at adapting Annihilation . It's the perfect epic for the MCU and could go a long way in making it as popular as it was before Avengers: Endgame .

2006 was a massive year for Marvel. Civil War was breaking the Marvel Universe , pitting hero against hero on Earth. For the first six years of the decade, Marvel was putting out some of the best books ever, but there was one part of the universe that was being woefully ignored and that was the cosmic side of the equation. The history of Cosmic Marvel is quite interesting; in the '60s, it was basically the baby of Lee and Kirby, the two of them setting up the basics like the Negative Zone, alien races like the Skrull, cosmic horrors like Galactus, and amazing heroes like Silver Surfer.

In the '70s, Cosmic Marvel was Adam Warlock and Captain Marvel battling the Magus, Thanos, and the High-Evolutionary, with writer/artist Jim Starlin orchestrating the best parts. Characters like the Guardians of the Galaxy, Moondragon, Gamora, Pip the Troll, Star-Lord, Rocket Raccoon, and more started to pop up. The '80s would see Cosmic Marvel fade when Starlin left the company, but when he returned in the beginning of the '90s, he would bring back his favorites and kick off the Infinity Trilogy, starting with Infinity Gauntlet.

'90s Cosmic Marvel was the Silver Surfer, Warlock and the Infinity Watch, and Thanos. However, the lackluster ending of the Infinity Trilogy would lead to Cosmic Marvel fading away again. That leads us up to 2006, when writer Keith Giffen, at the time also working on 52 , was part of a new Cosmic Marvel pitch, the one that would lead to Annihilation . The story saw something called the Annihilation Wave begin its runaway trip across the cosmos, destroying entire worlds.

In 2006, Cosmic Marvel was all but dead. The characters were all there, but no one had been using them. Giffen and writers Andy Lanning, Dan Abnett, Javier Grillo-Marxuach, and Simon Furman had their pick of characters and they started out with Silver Surfer, Nova, Super-Skrull, Ronan, and various living former Heralds of Galactus. It was a great mixture of characters, and fans ate the story up with a spoon. The Annihilation Wave was revealed to be under the control of the Fantastic Four villain Annihilus, the Kree betrayed everyone to team with him and survive, and even Galactus got involved in the war.

Annihilation was exactly the kind of big cosmic story that Cosmic Marvel did so well. I think one of the best ways to describe it is that it was old school and familiar, yet the story also felt fresh and new, partly because it was (Keith Giffen is one of our industry's greatest talents and he is dearly missed). Giffen and company were able to find the tone that made Cosmic Marvel work so well in the past – that sense of wonder and that anything could happen. The stakes were epic and fans loved it. It was a huge hit, helping Marvel further its lead in sales over DC, all while reintroducing classic characters. The story would birth numerous sequels and is responsible for the creation of the Guardians of the Galaxy that everyone knows and loves.

Marvel Studios has been doing better as of late, but the whole situation feels rather tenuous. If the next two Avengers movies can't stick the landing, it's not going to be great for the studio. However, I think that if the company wants something as close to a sure thing as possible, then Annihilation should be the direction they take the MCU. It has exactly the kind of big spectacle that the MCU does well and it's a more malleable story than most fans realize. Plus, Marvel already has all of the big pieces set up.

We have the Fantastic Four, who can open the Negative Zone. We have the Kree and the Skrull, whose conflict is key to the story. There's Galactus, Surfer, and the Guardians of the Galaxy. Down the road Thanos gets involved in the saga, which gives Marvel the chance to bring back its biggest villain. Annihilation would have to be changed in various ways to fit the MCU, but fans are used to that by now. There are lots of Marvel stories the MCU shouldn't adapt , but Annihilation isn't one of them.

The MCU was able to bring superheroes to the masses, trying to be as close to the comics as possible. It could have failed miserably, but Marvel Studios was able to pull it off. However, the last few years haven't been able to find the success that used to be commonplace for Marvel. There's still entertaining projects and massive hits, but it's just not the same. Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars are going to be hits (unless Doomsday is really bad; it's not probable, but it could happen), but Marvel needs a plan again.

Annihilation can give them that plan. Marvel looks like it's going to be focusing on the Fantastic Four and the X-Men in the future, but both of those franchises are great for cosmic adventures – an argument can be made that Fantastic Four (Vol. 1) and Uncanny X-Men (Vol. 1) were the epicenter of Cosmic Marvel after Starlin left in the '80s. Most importantly, Annihilation gives the MCU a direction, one that would hype fans up for all of the movies, not just the big ones. The MCU needs to expand and Annihilation can be the key to its future.

What do you think about Annihilation ? Do you want the MCU to adapt it or would you rather they go another direction after the Multiverse Saga? Sound off in the comments section below.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google CD Projekt Red has shared a new update this week on the development of its sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , and it sounds quite promising. Although The Witcher 4 is the main focus of CDPR right now , the studio hasn't shied away from the fact that it's working on a follow-up to Cyberpunk 2077 as well. And while we're likely still quite far away from seeing Cyberpunk 2 in action, the studio has now shared new information on where it's at in development.

Detailed in a new call with investors , CD Projekt Red VP Karolina Gnaś briefly touched on Cyberpunk 2 and how the project is going. Although Gnaś didn't say anything definitively about when the game would be shown off, she did say that CD Projekt Red is planning to staff up more heavily throughout 2027. The implication is that these new hires will be brought in to work specifically on Cyberpunk 2 , which suggests the game should enter production either next year or in 2028.

"[The team is] making good progress with Cyberpunk 2 , we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production," Gnaś said.

CD Projekt Red beginning full development on Cyberpunk 2 in 2028 would actually make a ton of sense, as this year is also the same one in which The Witcher 4 is planned to release . While The Witcher 4 will almost certainly continue to receive new content and updates after its arrival, much of CDPR will certainly begin shifting its focus to the studio's next major game, which will be that of Cyberpunk 2 .

Assuming that things play out in this manner, this would result in Cyberpunk 2 not actually releasing until well after 2030. Given the sheer scale that Cyberpunk 2 will certainly have, the game will almost certainly have to be in production for a period of three to five years. This puts it on track to not launch until the next generation of consoles becomes available.

Still, even if Cyberpunk 2 is this far down the road, CD Projekt Red could begin teasing it a bit sooner. The original Cyberpunk 2077 had its first teaser trailers emerge years before the game ever saw the light of day. While there's always the chance that CDPR might not want to go about things in this same way, it leaves the door open for Cyberpunk 2 being revealed in some capacity in the months or year to come.

How do you feel about Cyberpunk 2 based on what CDPR has said now? And when do you think that this ucpoming RPG will actually release? Be sure to let me know down in the comments section.
